Football.title: Turkey U21 boss rushed to hospital after falling on touchline during match
Football.content:
Turkey U21 boss rushed to hospital after falling on touchline during match

Turkey Under-21 manager Egemen Korkmaz collapsed during their Euros qualifying match against Croatia on Tuesday.

With around 34 minutes on the clock, Demir Ege Tiknaz was sent off for the hosts after picking up a second yellow card.

3 Medics rushed to treat Korkmaz after he collapsed Credit: Getty

His manager could be seen expressing his anger towards the referee for his decision and animatedly took his coat off.



However, he then appeared to fall to the ground and spark concern from his players and staff.

An ambulance made its way over to Korkmaz and provided treatment as his players and staff anxiously watched on.

The match was subsequently suspended.

In a statement, the Turkish Football Federation said: "Our U21 National Team Head Coach, Egemen Korkmaz, lost consciousness after slipping and hitting his head on the ground in the 35th minute of today's UEFA U21 European Championship group qualifying match against Croatia at the Opus Arena in Osijek.

"Korkmaz, who suffered swelling on his head due to the fall, received initial treatment from our medical team on the sidelines.



"He is conscious and has been taken to the hospital by ambulance for further examination. We wish him a speedy recovery."

Turkish giants Fenerbahce sent their best wishes to Korkmaz as they said: "Get well soon, Egemen Korkmaz.



"We regretfully learned that Egemen Korkmaz, the Head Coach of our U21 National Team, fell ill during the match and was taken to the hospital.

"We extend our get-well wishes to Egemen Korkmaz and hope for his swift recovery."



3 Korkmaz has since been taken to hospital Credit: Getty

Besiktas followed suit by adding: "We have learned with great sorrow that Egemen Korkmaz, the Head Coach of the U21 National Team, fell ill during the Croatia match and was taken to the hospital.

"We extend our wishes for a speedy recovery to Egemen Korkmaz and hope he regains his health as soon as possible."

U21 Euros qualifying so far

Korkmaz has not lost any matches during Turkey's qualifying campaign for the U21 Euros next year.

They are on course to qualify for the first time since 2000.

England are set to enter as the reigning champions after their 3-2 win over Germany in last year's final.



The Three Lions are currently top of their qualification group on 16 points with four matches to play.

3 Croatia and Turkey are both eyeing qualification for next summer's tournament Credit: Getty

Korkmaz's playing and coaching career

Korkmaz spent the majority of his playing career in his country's football league system.

He played for Fenerbahce, with whom he won the Turkish Super Lig, Turkish Cup and Turkish Super Cup.

Korkmaz, a centre-back, also played alongside Liverpool cult hero Dirk Kuyt at the club.



The 43-year-old also played for Besiktas, where he played against Stoke City in the 2011/12 Europa League campaign.

Korkmaz earned nine caps for Turkey, and played part in their qualification campaign for the 2014 World Cup.

After spells as an assistant at Denizlispor, Erzurumspor and Trabzonspor, he became the manager of Turkey's U21 side in May.

Football.title: Oliver Glasner insists he has no regrets over outburst with Premier League future in doubt
Football.content:
Oliver Glasner insists he has no regrets over outburst with Premier League future in doubt

Oliver Glasner has insisted he has no regrets over his emotional outburst in January where he hit out at Crystal Palace’s hierarchy.

The Eagles boss, who will leave the club at the end of the season, said he felt 'abandoned' at the club in a bombshell interview in January.

5 Glasner is set to depart Crystal Palace at the end of the season, after over two years in charge Credit: Getty

A day after announcing that captain Marc Guehi was set to leave for Manchester City and that he himself would not extend his contract, Glasner took aim at the Palace hierarchy.

Following a 2-1 defeat to Sunderland in their first match without Guehi, the Austrian slammed the timing of the sale 24 hours before a match, which left him without an immediate replacement.

His outburst came amid a dismal run of form, with Palace winless in ten at the time and they also suffered a humiliating FA Cup exit to non-league Macclesfield.

Results didn't get much better after his explosive comments in the media, and speculation began that Glasner could be sacked before the end of the season, with some fans turning on him.

But after turbulent start to 2026, his side have found form again recently, losing just once in their last six games in all competitions.

This includes an extra-time victory over Cypriot side AEK Larnaca in the Conference League to send the Eagles into the quarter-finals.

As the season reaches a crucial stage, Glasner remains in with a chance of clinching another trophy, after guiding the club to their first ever major honours with FA Cup glory last term. Palace then beat Liverpool in the Community Shield at the start of the season.

Glasner: Owners weren't pleased with bombshell interview

In an exclusive interview with talkSPORT's Jim White on the Outspoken podcast, Glasner was asked if have any regrets over his comments in the media.

To this, the 51-year-old replied: “I don't have regrets, honestly.

“I'm very honest. I never tell somebody what he wants to hear, I always tell them what is my opinion, what is my feeling. It doesn't mean that it's always right.

5 The timing of Guehi's £20million departure to Manchester City did not go down well with Glasner Credit: Getty

5 Glasner will leave Palace as their most successful manager in history having won two trophies Credit: Getty

“But I think everybody deserves to hear how I'm feeling, how I see some things that happened or that's going on.

“Not everybody has to be delighted with my opinion, to be honest.”

Despite insisting he wouldn't change anything, Glasner admitted his explosive comments weren't well received by the Palace owners.

talkSPORT reported at the time that his shock departure announcement had come as a surprise to senior figures at the club, who had been unaware beforehand of his plans to share the news.

Asked how the Eagles ownership responded to the saga, Glasner said: "Honestly, I think they were not really pleased.

"But we talked about it and they could understand me. I think the players, especially.

5 Glasner informed club chairman Steve Parish in October that he would be leaving Selhurst Park in the summer Credit: Getty

"For me, the most important part is always the players and they know me. They know that I'm honest and they could deal with it."

Reflecting on a turbulent period, Glasner defended his decision to air his frustrations over Guehi's exit, which he said the players felt too.

He added: “In this special moment, we felt it. I felt it, the players felt it.

"The day before a game with some injury concerns, for me, I had to get rid of it."

Insisting he shares the owners' ambitions, he added: “There is one main goal - we all want the best for Crystal Palace.

“It's the players, it's the manager, it's the staff and it's the chairman. And then it's important that not everybody says: ‘Yeah, it's good what you're doing’ because I think you need discussions that bring the club forward.

5 The Austrian has won both the FA Cup and Community Shield during his tenure Credit: Getty

“And I think when we look back at the two years where I'm in charge, we brought the club forward.”

What does the future hold?

With the end of his Crystal Palace tenure approaching, Glasner refused to shed much light on what could be next for him.

Asked if he would like to stay in the Premier League, he said: “To be honest, I don't know right now.

"For me, it's really the focus on having a great end to the season. We still have a lot to achieve. We're not too far away from the European places in the Premier League. We're in the quarter-final of a European competition.

“So now we're entering crunch time and we have to have the players fit. And so I'm really 100 per cent focused on the end of the season.

“And then what I learned in football, I've now been in football for more than 30 years - you can't plan anything. Things happen or they don't happen. So I'm really open and let's see what the summer brings.

“But again, for me, the most important thing is now having a great end to the season, having a great end to more than two years with Crystal Palace and then celebrating all together.”

Football.title: Tottenham told Roberto De Zerbi is a ‘fantastic character’ despite fan protest
Football.content:
The Tottenham Hotspur hierarchy can look forward to working with a character like Roberto De Zerbi.

That's according to Brighton chief executive Paul Barber as his former head coach begins a new challenge in north London.

4 De Zerbi has signed a five-year deal with Spurs with his first target steering them away from relegation trouble Credit: AFP

Spurs announced the appointment of De Zerbi on a five-year deal on Tuesday and talkSPORT understands the contract has no relegation clause.

He joins the relegation-threatened club just over a month after he left Marseille in France, and two years on from his Brighton exit.

De Zerbi was a huge success on the south coast as he guided them to Europe for the first time in their 124-year-history at the end of the 2022/23 season.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Barber expressed his confidence in the 46-year-old's ability to make an impact at Spurs.

"Roberto is a fabulous football coach and I'm sure wherever he goes, he will do very well," he told Jim White.

When asked about their differences at the end of their time working together, a mutual exit, Barber added: "Not differences as such.

"Roberto did two fabulous years with us, we got into Europe for the first time in the club's history.

"We worked really hard to entertain the fans, which we did.

"And Roberto is a fantastic character to work with.

"Obviously we wished him well when he went to Marseille, and let's see what the future brings for him."

4 De Zerbi has a 'fantastic character, according to Brighton chief Barber Credit: Getty

Spurs fan protests against De Zerbi

Amid the speculation over De Zerbi and his move to Spurs, women's fan group Women of The Lane hit out at the club's appointment.

De Zerbi was Marseille manager when they signed Mason Greenwood from Manchester United in July 2024.

Greenwood was previously charged with attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour.

These charges were dropped in February 2023, with De Zerbi calling the former United forward a 'good guy' in November.

"He's a good guy, he paid a heavy price for what happened, a very heavy price," he said in quotes per the Daily Telegraph.

In a statement posted last week, Women of The Lane expressed their opposition to De Zerbi amid his comments on Greenwood.

4 A Spurs fan group have hit out at De Zerbi for his comments on Greenwood Credit: Getty

"There is growing speculation linking Spurs with Roberto De Zerbi," they said.

"We want to be clear about how this is landing with many women and allies in our community.

"De Zerbi has publicly defended Mason Greenwood in a way that downplays the seriousness of male violence against women and girls.

"That raises serious questions about judgement and leadership.

"Clubs signal their values through the decisions they make. Who they appoint matters. The manager sets the tone, every day, for what is expected, what is tolerated, and how people are treated.

"At a time when Spurs needs to rebuild, that culture matters as much as anything on the pitch.

4 De Zerbi is tasked with keeping Spurs in the Premier League Credit: Getty

"For many in our community, this is difficult to reconcile with the club's stated commitments to respect, safety and inclusion.

"This is not an appointment Tottenham Hotspur should make. It introduces unnecessary cultural risk without a clear, proven track record to justify it.

"No to De Zerbi."

News.title: Keir Starmer says ‘closer’ ties with EU is only way to tackle Iran war ‘storm’ as he brushes off Trump Nato threat
News.content:
EU WHAT? Keir Starmer says ‘closer’ ties with EU is only way to tackle Iran war ‘storm’ as he brushes off Trump Nato threat

THE Iran war means Britain must move closer to the EU, Sir Keir Starmer declared this morning.

The PM brushed off threats from Donald Trump to pull out of Nato, arguing “our long term national interest” requires moving closer to Europe.





It came after the President blasted the military alliance as a “paper tiger” and said removing the US has become “beyond consideration”.

Responding to the threat, the PM said: “It is increasingly clear that as the world continues down this volatile path, our long-term national interest requires closer partnership with our allies in Europe.

“The UK will not just ratify existing commitments made at last year’s summit.



“We want to be more ambitious, closer economic closer, security, closer economic cooperation, closer security cooperation, a partnership that recognises our shared values, our shared interest and our shared future, a partnership for the dangerous world that we must navigate together.”

Sir Keir added that an EU summit will be held in the coming weeks to “ratify existing commitments”.

Earlier today Mr Trump said the war would be over in “two or three weeks”.

The President claimed US troops would end their assault with or without a deal.



He said: “I think we’re … two or three weeks.

“We leave because there’s no reason for us to do this … We’re finishing the job and I think within maybe two weeks, maybe a couple of days longer, to do the job.

“When we feel for a long period of time they are put into the Stone Ages and cannot have a nuclear weapon, we will leave.”

The Iran war has dropped a cost of living bombshell on Brits – with energy bills jumping by £288 a year and diesel pushing £2 a litre.

Drivers have already been stung for an extra £544million since the conflict began as Tehran’s stranglehold on oil supplies continues to hike pump prices.



Under-pressure Sir Keir held another emergency COBR meeting yesterday on ways to ease the economic shocks from hammering family finances.

Households are facing a sharp rise in gas and electricity costs this summer, with Cornwall Insight warning the price cap for a typical dual fuel home could hit £1,929 between July and September after falling to £1,641 today.

That would mark an 18 per cent increase on the April level, with the surge in wholesale prices already baked into the next calculation.

Meanwhile, the costs for homes reliant on heating oil, which are not covered by the Ofgem cap, have already soared.

Government figures showed the average price per litre of standard grade burning oil stood at 104.1p in March, nearly double the average in February of 53.5p and the highest monthly figure since official data began in January 1989.



Analysts say there is little sign of costs dropping back to pre-war levels any time soon while Iran keeps its grip on the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and gas supplies.

Disruption there has sent gas prices soaring and pushed crude oil above $100 dollars a barrel since the conflict began on February 28.

The pain is being felt just as sharply at the pumps, where the cost of filling a typical 55-litre family car with diesel reached £100.52 for the first time in more than three years on Tuesday.

Average diesel prices at UK forecourts reached 182.8p per litre on Tuesday, representing a 40p jump since the start of the Middle East crisis.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The average cost of petrol has also climbed to 152.8p per litre, an increase of 20p since the war began. Motoring research charity the RAC Foundation estimated that these rapid rises in pump prices have already led to motorists paying an additional £544million for fuel.



It means the Treasury has raked in an extra £90.6million in what the RAC calls a “VAT war windfall”.

News.title: White influencer Lauren Blake accused of photoshopping her face onto black creator’s body in bizarre ‘deepfake pic’
News.content:
A WHITE influencer with over one million followers has been accused of photoshopping her face onto a black creator’s body.

Tatiana Elizabeth, who is African-American, took to TikTok this week to explain to her 350,000 followers how Lauren Blake Boultier had lifted her likeness.





Elizabeth attended the 2024 US Open in New York, sharing an image of herself dressed in a tennis-inspired outfit.

To her amazement, she then saw the very same photograph on Boultier’s feed two years later.

“So, this photo to the right is a photo of me at the US Open in 2024,” Elizabeth said.

“This photo to the left is a photo I came across this morning on Instagram of someone who castrated me and decided to use my image and my environment.”

Side by side, the two photos look almost identical – except for the face.

Boultier’s version features the same outfit, including a Louis Vuitton handbag, and even the same pose.

Perhaps the most telling clue is that Boultier has the same tattoo on her right wrist.

“Bar for bar, the weirdest part about this is that it’s not even an AI influencer,” Elizabeth said.



“This is a real person who used AI to put her head on my body.”

To make matters worse, Boultier tagged the location as the recently finished Miami Open – even though it is clearly the Arthur Ashe Stadium in Queens.

To that end, global tennis superstar Coco Gauff commented: “this court is not even in Miami…”

“By no means am I trying to bash this girl. Mental health is real, and I’m not a bully,” Elizabeth said.

“I’m just a little perplexed. I just want to know the reason.



“Has social media gotten into our heads so much that we are disregarding couth?”

Elizabeth said she has not heard anything from Boultier, despite commenting on her picture.

“She has not apologised, she has not given an explanation, and she is probably embarrassed but I think that the nice and accountable thing to do would be to reach out and at least apologise to the person whose photo you took,” she said.

Unsurprisingly, Elizabeth has since deleted the controversial image.

This strange incident fits into a broader category of behaviour exhibited by “virtual influencers“.



These AI-generated content creators often stick electronically-generated faces on real models‘ bodies.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Many of these accounts are often linked to OnlyFans models, offering paid subscriptions for sexually explicit content.

Face-swap apps have also become more popular, allowing users to create deepfakes directly on their phones.

News.title: Trump to address world tonight after vow to end Iran war in DAYS…with or without a deal & whether Hormuz reopens or not
News.content:
DONALD Trump is expected to address the world tonight with an “important” update as he vows to end the Iran war in days.

The US President told reporters on Tuesday he will leave Iran in “two or three weeks”, with or without a deal.





He also suggested he does not care if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and will shift responsibility of the vital trade route to those who rely on it.

Earlier this week, Trump threatened to “obliterate” Iranian energy sites if a peace deal was not agreed, but insisted negotiations were making progress.

He reiterated his claim that regime change in Iran has “been achieved”, and the US is just “finishing the job”.

As the world waits with baited breath, Tehran has continued its unrelenting blitz of gulf nations.

The rogue state hit a tanker off the coast of Qatar and Kuwait International Airport on Wednesday.

Warning sirens rung out across Israel overnight as came under fire from both Yemen and Iran.

It comes as the US unleashed huge bunker buster bombs on an ammunition depot in the Iranian city of Isfahan.



The US has been under growing pressure to end the war as Iran’s iron grip on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has caused oil prices to skyrocket, with a barrel of Brent crude reaching $118 on Tuesday.

Iran has throttled the Persian Gulf chokehold – through with 20 per cent of the worlds oil passes through – since US-Israeli forces began their bombing campaign on Tehran.

The US has presented Iran with a 15-point plan in a bid for peace, which demanded for the strait to be reopened.

Iran responded with its own five-point ceasefire agreement, including sovereignty over the key waterway.



On Tuesday Trump suggested the war could be brought to an end with Iran controlling the Strait.

The US “will not have anything to do with” what happens to the Strait of Hormuz, he said.

He told the UK and other fuel-starved nations that they can either buy from the US or “build up some delayed courage, go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT”.

Prime Minister Keir Starmer is expected to hold an urgent press conference on Wednesday as Brits face paying more than £100 to fill up their cars.

Iran’s national security committee approved proposals to toll ships passing through the strait on Monday, according to Iran’s state media.



Select vessels are currently charged an eyewatering £1.5million to pass through.

And the passage will not be reopened for American vessels.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the committee, said on X: “Trump has finally achieved his dream of ‘regime change’ – but in the region’s maritime regime!

“The Strait of Hormuz will certainly reopen, but not for you; it will be open for those who comply with the new laws of Iran. The 47 years of hospitality are over forever.”

The conflict in the Middle East has piled strain onto Trump’s relationship with Europe after US allies failed to join the war despite the deepening fuel shortage crisis.



The president told The Telegraph on Wednesday that he is strongly considering pulling the US out of Nato as a result.

Branding the defence treaty as a “paper tiger”, he said removing America from the alliance was now “beyond reconsideration”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Taking a fresh swipe at the UK, the president rebuked Starmer for failing to intervene in the war.

“You don’t even have a navy. You’re too old and had aircraft carriers that didn’t work,” he said, referring to the state of Britain’s fleet of warships.

News.title: Trump says he’s on verge of pulling US out of Nato as ‘like Putin’ he knows alliance is ‘paper tiger’…& UK ‘has no navy’
News.content:
DONALD Trump has said the US is on the verge of leaving Nato after the alliance’s “terrible” show of support in the Middle East.

America’s withdrawal could spell disaster for Western security chiefs as they scramble to shore up their nation’s defences without the additional £3.8trillion of US military might.





Sir Keir Starmer has staunchly defended Nato as “the single most effective military alliance the world has ever seen” after Trump’s bombshell threat, adding that the UK would review its security ties with the EU.

But Trump has repeatedly blasted America’s allies for their inaction in the ongoing conflict, and claimed that like Russian tyrant Vladimir Putin, he knows that Nato is a “paper tiger”.

He yesterday branded the alliance as “terrible”, telling fuel-starved members “get your own oil” after they failed to send warships and help release the Strait of Hormuz from Iran’s grip.



Asked by the Telegraph if he would reconsider the alliance, Trump said: “Oh yes, I would say [it’s] beyond reconsideration.

“I was never swayed by Nato. I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way.”

Washington has poured countless resources into the weeks-long mission to free the vital 24-mile waterway with oil prices shooting up with every day Tehran maintains a foothold.

And despite the fuel shortage threatening a global recession, Nato has been reluctant to actively involve itself int he conflict.



“Beyond not being there, it was actually hard to believe,” Trump told the Telegraph of Nato’s response.

“And I didn’t do a big sale. I just said, ‘Hey’, you know, I didn’t insist too much. I just think it should be automatic.

“We’ve been there automatically, including Ukraine.

“Ukraine wasn’t our problem. It was a test, and we were there for them, and we would always have been there for them.

“They weren’t there for us.”



The president singled out the UK, suggesting that the Royal Navy was no longer a competent threat.

“You don’t even have a navy. You’re too old and had aircraft carriers that didn’t work,” he said of Britain’s fleet.

It comes after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth mocked the “big, bad Royal Navy” yesterday, saying it should be prepared to step up.

If Trump was to follow through with his threat, it would send the UK and Nato members into a tail spin as they to

What is Nato? THE North Atlantic Treaty Organisation is a political and military alliance of countries from North America and Europe. It was founded in 1949 to counter the Soviet Union with Cold War tensions rising. Among articles in its founding treaty is the principle of collective defence – the idea that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all of them. Nato takes decisions by consensus but the political and military strength of the United States means that it is by far the most powerful country in the alliance. Its nuclear arsenal is seen as the ultimate security guarantee. Nato has 31 members – most of them European nations, plus the United States and Canada. The newest member is Finland, which joined last April in reaction to Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Sweden applied to join along with Finland but is waiting for Hungary to ratify its application as the final major step before membership.

News.title: Woman attacked by WOLF on busy shopping street outside Ikea with beast mauling her face after she tried to lead it away
News.content:
SAVAGED IN STREET Woman attacked by WOLF on busy shopping street outside Ikea with beast mauling her face after she tried to lead it away

A WOMAN has been attacked by a wolf outside an Ikea in a horrific city attack.

The wild beast mauled the woman’s face while she was trying to lead it away from other shoppers in Hamburg, Germany.





Authorities had been hunting the savage animal for days after receiving countless sightings of a lone wolf in the city.

The young wolf was spotted on Monday evening in the bustling Grosse Bergstrasse, part of the main shopping district of Altona.

Just 2.5 miles from the city centre, the beast was clearly disoriented – repeatedly running into a glass wall in an arcade.

The woman, 65, was trying to free the predator when she was reportedly bitten on the left side of her face.

She was bleeding from a wound at the corner of her mouth and cheek and required stitches, Bild reported.

The wolf fled across Hamburg before it jumped into the Inner Alster lake.

Police spent about an hour trying to snare the animal and they had to arm themselves with shields.



It has not yet been decided what will happen to the young animal but it is currently in veterinary care.

The “rare” attack raises concerns around the reintroduction of the endangered predator to Germany three decades ago.

It’s understood to be the first physical attack on a human since 1998.

Forest and wildlife specialist Dr. Andreas Kinser told Bild the attack was “unprecedented”.

“This is the first known case of a wolf penetrating deep into the city centre,” he said.



Dr Kinser said as the population of wild wolves grow, so too does the pressure on forest resources which may draw them closer to the city.

He added: “Young animals are very curious – much like puppies.”

Last week, the German government passed laws to allow wolves to be hunted in order to manage their population and protect livestock.

Federal Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said wolves “must be allowed to stay”, the BBC reported.

“It is not a question of driving the wolf away again, but of finding viable ways to live peacefully alongside it,” he said.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Wolf hunting season is scheduled to run from 1 July to 31 October.

News.title: Married finance boss who splashed £160k of ‘stolen cash’ on escorts including Britain’s ‘best paid porn star’ faces jail
News.content:
LOCKED UP Married finance boss who splashed £160k of ‘stolen cash’ on escorts including Britain’s ‘best paid porn star’ faces jail

A MARRIED finance boss who splashed £160,000 of “stolen” cash on escorts including Britain’s “best paid porn star” has been jailed.

Mohammed Asif Khan was accused of “stealing” about £1.1million of company money while working for North of England Coachworks.





The “self-styled director of finance” splashed around £160,000 on payments to escorts, a court heard.

This included £56,000 on £1,000-an-hour call girl Gemma Massey, who previously dated Towie star Kirk Norcross and was once dubbed Britain’s “best paid porn star”.

In 2024, he agreed to hand the company a £500,000 payout in order to settle a civil claim against him.

Khan accepted he owes the money “in respect of the frauds and fraudulent breaches of trust as alleged against him in this action”.



But he has still paid back only around £550 of that pawning a £20,000 Rolex watch to prevent his ex-bosses getting it.

As a result, the dad-of-two has now been sentenced to six months in jail for contempt of court.

But High Court judge Mr Justice Jay postponed Khan being imprisoned until April 17 to allow him time to lodge an appeal.

The court previously heard Khan worked for North of England Coachworks until 2019 in a financial and managerial role.



But when serious irregularities with cheque payments and money transfers were noticed, he was quizzed and resigned, the firm’s barrister Sam Neaman said.

He said investigations revealed that Khan had been using company cheques and transfers to pay for things that were not for the firm’s benefit.

The net loss was valued at around £1.1million – with an estimated £160,000 of that going to named women including Gemma, Mr Neaman said.

He added: “It is not just names, you will see an awful lot of information from the internet which establishes what these ladies did for a profession.

“[Gemma] is obviously one of many.”



The court previously heard that Gemma – a former dental nurse and beautician – was “self-described as a high class escort” on a webpage put forward as part of the case.

Gemma once boasted on the BBC of being the UK’s highest paid porn queen.

Khan admitted his “shame” after using company money to pay escorts but insisted he did not do anything his employers did not approve of.

Quizzed in the witness box whether his bosses had given him permission to spend money on prostitutes, Mr Khan said: “Not specifically for that, but they were aware. In reality, they didn’t care what I spent that money on.

“The G Massey name was on there. They knew that was what I was doing.”



He agreed that judgment be entered against him in favour of the company in the sum of £500,000, which he was to pay by 4pm on 6 August 2024.

But the court heard that he has paid only around £550 despite pawning his Rolex Daytona, which he was specifically banned from “dealing with” by a freezing injunction.

The money loaned against it was paid into a bank account, which he had not disclosed the existence of, before being transferred into his wife’s business to go towards a property purchase.

When his former employers discovered the watch had been pawned, they launched proceedings to have him committed to prison for contempt of court.

Giving his judgment, Mr Justice Jay said: “The act of pawning it was intended to place the watch outside the immediate custody and control of Mr Khan.



“He must have been aware that disposing of the loan monies from his account to his wife’s company account was a breach of the order.

“The seriousness of the matter is compounded by loan monies being paid into a bank account Mr Khan had not previously disclosed.

“I am far from convinced that he does fully appreciate the seriousness of the breach.

“I have come to the conclusion that I wouldn’t be performing my public duty if I suspended Mr Khan’s sentence.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I have carefully reflected on this. I appreciate that he has considerable personal mitigation in the form of a supportive wife, two young children and he has remunerative employment.



“I am duty bound to impose an immediate custodial sentence in this case.”

News.title: Horror moment journalist who worked for BBC is kidnapped ‘by pro-Iran militia’ before dramatic chase and rollover crash
News.content:
THIS is the harrowing moment foreign correspondent Shelly Kittleson was abducted in Iraq by a suspected Iran-linked group.

Footage circulating on social media shows the American journalist being bundled into a car by armed men near Baghdad Hotel on Saadoun Street on Tuesday evening.





Filmed from across a busy intersection, the ambush marks a dangerous development for Westerners in Iraq, particularly for reporters.

Kataib Hezbollah – the most powerful of the Shiite, Iran-backed groups that hold sway in Iraq – is believed to be behind the attack as part of an alleged plot to capture or kill female journalists.

Kittleson’s emergency contact Alex Plitsas, CNN national security analyst, confirmed her capture in a statement on X.



“I can confirm that my friend Shelly Kittleson was abducted and may have taken hostage in Baghdad by Khatib Hezbollah,” he said.

“Whereabouts and condition unknown. I am her designated US point of contact. If you have information please provide to law enforcement and send me a DM.”

He later told CBS that Kittleson had been warned by the US government about a specific threat to her from Iran-backed paramilitaries.

Plitsas said his friend had been warned that her name was on a list in the militia’s possession.



A second source confirmed that the journalist had been told of a risk, but thought it was false information.

What we know about Kataib Hezbollah IRAQ's most powerful paramilitaries, Kataib Hezbollah, is believed to be behind the kidnapping of the journalist. Founded in 2014 to stop lighting advances by ISIS at the time, it is now one of the largest groups within the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), which itself is an Iranian-backed paramilitary umbrella group that operates within Iraq. Over the years, the militia has been linked to attacks on American troops, diplomatic missions, and foreign nationals. Its influence extends way beyond military operations, making it a significant player in Iraq’s internal power dynamics. Kataib Hezbollah has repeatedly called for the removal of US forces and has been accused of carrying out attacks aligned with that objective. Before the conflict in the Middle East broke out at the end of February, it had warned of a “total war” if Iran is attacked. Chief Abu Hussein al‑Hamidawi issued a fiery statement, calling on fighters to be prepared for war. The militia has been accused of a long list of human rights violations – extrajudicial killings, abductions and forced disappearances of 1,500 Sunni boys and men in Jurf al-Sakhar area of Iraq.

The Iraqi Interior Ministry said an operation was launched immediately based on what it called “precise intelligence.”

Security forces chased the reporter’s captors in a mad pursuit that ended in one of their cars overturning and the arrest of one suspect.

Kittleson was not inside and a frantic search to trace her continues.

The US State Department later revealed that the man taken into custody had ties to Kataib Hezbollah.



Without naming Kittleson, US Assistant Secretary of State Dylan Johnson said in a statement: “An individual with ties to the Iranian-aligned militia group Kataib Hizballah believed to be involved in the kidnapping has been taken into custody by Iraqi authorities.

“Iraq remains at a Level 4 Travel Advisory and Americans are advised not to travel to Iraq for any reason and to leave Iraq now.”

The kidnapping recalls that of Russian-Israeli researcher Elizabeth Tsurkov at a Baghdad cafe in March 2023.

She was held hostage by Kataib Hezbollah for 903 days, during which she suffered extreme abuse, leaving her physically and mentally scarred.

Tsurkov was freed in September 2025 under a deal that was brokered by the US.



No group has claimed responsibility for the abduction of the freelance journalist yet.

Kittleson, based in Rome, Italy, has covered conflicts in Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria.

Plitsas described her as “one of the kindest people” who “doesn’t have a mean bone in her body.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Shelly is a journalist who has lived and worked in the region and Central Asia for nearly two decades,” he added.

“She has been thoroughly vetted in Iraq and the Popular Mobilisation Forces know she’s a civilian.”

News.title: Feral youths swarm shops in UK cities after ‘link-ups’ fuelled by social media as terrified families locked in stores
News.content:
FERAL youths are sparking chaos in UK cities, storming shops and terrifying families with “linkups” fuelled by social media.

Groups of marauding teens yesterday tore through Clapham High Street, London, for a second time as similar scenes were seen in Birmingham on the first day of the Easter holidays.





Videos posted to social media in the aftermath of the incidents saw teens boasting that they had attended the chaotic scenes in London and Birmingham.

On Saturday, mobs of youths ran wild through both Clapham high street, London, and Birmingham city centre as groups of teens flooded the areas.

The incidents on Saturday saw the Marks and Spencer on Clapham high street looted after teens gathered en masse amd stormed the store.

Two teen girls aged 16 and one 15-year-old were arrested on suspicion of shoplifting and assault after the incident in London on Saturday.



While the chaotic scenes unfolded in the capital a similar incident occurred in Birmingham with footage showing a gaggle of dozens of teens marauding through the city centre.

Video of the chaos was shared online after the “linkup” in the UK’s second city which appeared to have been captured by a member of the mob.

A security guard has since told how he was forced to lock a family in a shop as the youngsters ran wild through Clapham High Street for a second time last night.

Anticipating further disorder, cops warned shopkeepers in advance of yesterday’s chaos, telling them to lock their doors ahead of the “linkup.”



Clips circulating on social media showed mobs of dozens of teens gathering in Clapham, south London.

The group reportedly terrorised locals as police vehicles arrived and officers desperately tried to bring the disorder to an end.

A dispersal order was put in place with the force confirming two teen girls were arrested on suspicion of assaulting an emergency worker during the frenzy.

Following last night’s incident, a Marks and Spencer security guard told The Daily Mail: “Police warned us there would be chaos, so we prepared for it because of what happened last Saturday.

“There were loads of kids sprinting and shouting and police advised all the shops to close for one hour.”



Shop security guard Mohammed went on to say the supermarket was forced to close the Clapham branch early and not reopen.

When the doors were locked up ahead of the disorder some customers were left trapped inside.



Police allegedly warned Mohammed and his colleagues in advance that the mobs would storm the area in a repeat of Saturday’s incident.

The security guard said: “They [police] said it would start at around 4pm so they were here since midday. But the chaos happened at 7pm. We had to lock shoppers in, at 8.15pm we let them out one by one with police and security holding the doors shut and escorting them out.”

Shoppers were left terrified, the security guard said, one woman with a pram and a baby reportedly had to be escorted to safety by responding cops.

According to the M&S worker a branch of Boots on the high street wasn’t as well prepared and was targeted by the mob of teens.

A Waitrose, McDonald’s and Sainsbury’s were all forced to close their doors early as the gang of yobs descended on the area.



Video footage from the scene showed groups of youngsters with balaclavas covering their faces gathered outside the stores on the high street.

Marked and unmarked police cars raced to the scene as the mob claimed control of the high street.

Cops were finally able to disperse the gathered teens at around 10:30pm.

During the chaos, traffic was brought to a standstill, fires were seen burning on nearby Clapham Common and commuters were forced to find refuge.

The chaos saw a group of around 60 teens facing down cops as officers tried to disperse the crowds.



Insults were hurled at the officers as teens ran past them and continued their anti-social behaviour.

A spokesman for the Metropolitan Police said of last night’s incident: “Police are responding to an ongoing incident on Clapham High Street following reports of a large crowd of young people causing anti-social behaviour.

“Officers are on the scene, and a dispersal order has been put in place, meaning anyone congregating must leave the area.

“At this time two teenage girls have been arrested on suspicion of assaulting an emergency worker. They have been taken to custody.

“Officers will remain in the area to offer support and respond to any concerns from local residents and businesses.”



Following the incidents on Saturday in Birmingham and London, teens posted clips of the disorder to social media, seemingly boasting that they were in attendance.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Saturday’s frenzied scenes occurred on the first day of the Easter holidays with teens mostly away from school.

The Sun has contacted the Met Police and West Midlands Police for comment.

News.title: Donald Trump threatens to pull out of NATO in biggest tantrum yet after embarrassing Iran war
News.content:
Donald Trump threatens to pull out of NATO in biggest tantrum yet after embarrassing Iran war

Donald Trump has labelled NATO a 'paper tiger' as he says it is 'beyond reconsideration' to withdraw America from the alliance treaty after members refused to send ships to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

View 3 Images Donald Trump has threatened to pull the US out of NATO (Image: The White House/AFP via Getty Im)

President Donald Trump has threatened to pull the US out of NATO, labelling the alliance a "paper tiger" after it failed to jump into America's war with Iran.

‌



The Republican leader said removing America from the treaty was now "beyond reconsideration" in the strongest indication so far about Trump's seriousness to withdraw from NATO. It comes after NATO allies refused to follow Trump's demands that they send warships to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

‌



NATO countries have been reluctant to send ships to help reopen the strait, which has been effectively closed by Tehran for weeks as tensions rise in the Middle East. With the Strait of Hormuz seeing around 20 per cent of the world's oil travelling through it, it has sparked a surge in global oil and gas prices while threatening a global recession.

‌



View 3 Images Trump made the comments after NATO allies declined to send warships to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Asked by the Telegraph if he would reconsider the US being a NATO member after the Iran conflict, he said: "Oh yes, I woud say [it's] beyond reconsideration. I was never swayed by NATO. I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way."

Regarding the reluctance from NATO members to heed his demands, he said: "Beyond not being there, it was actually hard to believe. And I didn't do a big sale. I just said 'Hey', you know, i didn't insist too much.

‌



"I just think it should be automatic. We've been there automatically, including Ukraine. Ukraine wasn't our problem. It was a test, and we were there for them, and we would always have been there for them. They weren't there for us."

View 3 Images Trump referenced how the US was 'automatically' there for Ukraine (Image: Getty Images)

Hitting out at the UK directly after Sir Keir Starmer refused to get involved in the war against Iran launched by the US and Israel, Trump suggested that the UK's Royal Navy was not up to the task. He said: "You don't even have a navy. You're too old and had aircraft carrier that didn't work."

Article continues below

Trump went on to say that he wasn't going to "tell [Keir Starmer] what to do" when it came to the country's defence budget. He added: "He can do whatever he wants. It doesn't matter. All Starmer wants is costly windmills that are driving your energy prices through the roof."

Business Secretary Peter Kyle branded Trump a "very unconventional president" after Trump's tantrum over the lack of NATO support for his war efforts. Speaking on Sky News he said: "We have a very unconventional president, he uses the bully pulpit on social media very effectively.

"He dominates a lot of debate. Let's just see what actually happens. We do hear a lot of rhetoric from the President on social media. He uses rhetoric to destabilise; he uses rhetoric in order to keep people on their toes. We are very much in touch with the American administration."

News.title: Homeowners rip up carpets in Victorian home and hearts sink
News.content:
Homeowners rip up carpets in Victorian home and hearts sink

Homeowners who are renovating their Victorian home ripped up the carpets in their hallway and were left devastated by what they found underneath - as it wasn't what they expected

View Image The couple couldn't believe what was underneath their carpets (stock photo) (Image: Getty Images)

Renovating a home comes with risks. If you're planning extensive renovations to your property, such as ripping out your old kitchen or putting in an extension, there are a number of things you need to give some serious thought to before building work can commence so you don't end up accidentally bursting a pipe or knocking a hole into the wrong wall.

‌



You also shouldn't set your expectations too high when renovating an old house, as one couple on social media recently found out. The homeowners are in the process of renovating their Victorian home, and had been hoping to find some traditional period features they can restore.

‌



Ripping up carpets in old homes in the hope of finding stunning Victorian-era tiles has become hugely popular on social media in recent months, so when Fil and Kiara moved into their fixer-upper home in December 2025, they began documenting their renovation journey on TikTok.

‌



In a recent video, the couple decided to take the plunge and find out what sort of floor was lurking underneath the old carpets, knowing there could be a chance that Victorian tiles lay beneath.

But their hearts sank when they pulled back the carpet to find orange-tinged tiles straight from the 1970s.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



They wrote on their video: "We were expecting Victorian tiles... we got THIS instead. The 70s owe us an apology."

Commenters on the post were immediately concerned for the couple, with some warning it is possible the tiles could contain asbestos. If the property was built or renovated before the 1980s, any tiles should be treated as suspicious.

Asbestos is a group of naturally occurring, fibrous silicate minerals known for their strength and heat resistance. These properties previously made asbestos a popular construction material for things like insulation and tiles, but inhaling fibres can cause severe lung diseases and cancers.

‌



The only way to know for sure whether the tiles contain asbestos is to have them professionally tested, which Fil and Kiara have said they are in the process of doing. But until then, they have insisted they won't be touching any of the tiles, as breaking them or attempting to remove them could release the dangerous fibres.

Responding to one commenter asking about asbestos, they said: "We don’t know, we will need to get it tested eventually. For now we have avoided drilling, breaking, or attempting removal until further investigation."

Other commenters on the post offered their sympathies to the couple, noting that it's always disheartening to realise that your home doesn't have the cool features you thought it might when you bought it.

Article continues below

One person said: "Gutted." Another added: "That sucks, I'm sorry."

Before ripping up your carpets in the search for Victorian tiles, it's important to know when your house was built. Fil and Kiara claim their property was likely built between the late 1800s and early 1900s, which puts them right at the end of the era for Victorian-style tiles.

Intricate star or checkerboard patterns are most likely to be found in terraced houses built between 1860 and 1900, while simpler, geometric tiled designs were more common in Edwardian properties built between 1901 and 1910.

News.title: Norfolk factory pest control workers found dead with frozen hands and faces
News.content:
Norfolk factory pest control workers found dead with frozen hands and faces

Neil Moon, 49, and Jonathan 'Jon' Collins, 34, were tragically found dead on a pest control job at Banham Poultry in Norfolk after unknowingly walking through a pathway filled with toxic gas

View 3 Images The scene outside Banham Poultry in Norfolk (Image: Harry Hubbard / SWNS.com)

The frozen bodies of two pest control workers were discovered after the pair unknowingly stepped into a factory filled with toxic gas, a court heard.

‌



Neil Moon, 49, and Jonathan 'Jon' Collins, 34, were tragically found dead at Banham Poultry in Norfolk in the early hours of October 4, 2018, after panicked relatives phoned the police when they failed to return home.

‌



The victim's families say their lives have "changed forever" after learning the men died from asphyxiation when nitrogen gas built up in a narrow pathway at the side of the chicken factory. Norwich Crown Court heard the men had entered the walkway while carrying out routine pest control work.

‌



There were no warning signs to indicate they were stepping into lethal gas, the court heard, with prosecutors describing the incident as a "cavalier" safety failure.

Prosecutor Craig Hassall KC said: "Ultimately, they were killed by a colourless, odourless gas. When they walked into the passageway they were given no warning of the risks."

View 3 Images Neil Moon, 49, was described as a 'devoted family man' (Image: SWNS.com)

‌



The men's bodies were found at around 1am in the one-man-width corridor between the factory and nearby railway tracks, with evidence of frozen hands and faces.

CCTV footage played to the court showed the pair arriving at the factory at around 8.30am. They were last seen alive at 11.40am. Relatives reported the men missing after they failed to return home that evening, sparking a search which led to the horror discovery.

The toxic gas had come from a dislodged duct pipe connected to a chilling system that the factory used to process chickens, the court heard.

‌



Mr Hassall told the court: "When these men entered the passageway ducting had become detached, pumping concentrated nitrogen into a narrow space."

Concerns had been raised in the past about mist drifting across railway platforms near the site, the hearing was told.

View 3 Images Jonathan 'Jon' Collins, 34, was described as an 'amazing father' (Image: SWNS.com)

‌



This led to a number of changes to the system in the months before the men were found. But Mr Hassall said the work had not been carried out safely, arguing the company had failed to protect workers on site.

Banham Poultry Limited and Air Products plc have admitted health and safety offences on the basis that the breaches caused the deaths.

The men's families spoke of their devastation in emotional statements read to the court. Jon's wife Gillian said: "My life stopped but I had to find the strength to carry on for our son."

‌



"I still don't know why it has taken these companies seven a half years to accept responsibility for causing these deaths," she added. "The careless and reckless actions of those responsible have had catastrophic consequences."

Their daughter Dakota described Jon as an "amazing father". She added: "My dad was a kind and caring man just doing his job. They were robbed of their lives."

Neil's fiancée Sara Dutton described him as a "strong and devoted family man", adding: "My life and the lives of my children changed forever. Our grief has not diminished over time. I have had seven years just treading water. Not really living, just waiting for the truth."

Article continues below

The sentencing hearing is due to conclude after two days.

News.title: Schoolgirl, 7, found dead in pond after mum found new childminder 'on Facebook'
News.content:
Schoolgirl, 7, found dead in pond after mum found new childminder 'on Facebook'

'Sweet' seven-year-old Nyla May Bradshaw was found dead in a pond near Doncaster shortly after going missing - her mum's friend said she had just found a new childminder on Facebook

View 2 Images Nyla May Bradshaw, seven, was found dead in a pond (Image: Facebook)

Family friends of a girl tragically found dead in a pond say the mum had been recommended a new child minder on Facebook just days before.

‌



Seven-year-old Nyla May Bradshaw was discovered in a pond at Owston Hall golf course, near Doncaster, on Monday. The girl, who was autistic, had been reported missing from the village of Skellow at 9.50am that same day.

‌



Tributes have rushed in from devastated family members, including Nyla's mum Hailey, who described her as her "sweet little girl". Charlotte Emma, best friends with Nyla’s mother, has now revealed that Hailey had asked a local Facebook group for help finding a childminder, and had been recommended someone who claimed to be an autism specialist.

‌



But within two hours, the mum is said to have received a text telling her Nyla was missing - and she was found in the pond shortly after.

View 2 Images Nyla's dad said she was his 'best friend and amazing daughter' (Image: Gofundme)

‌



'Sweet' missing girl found dead at Owston Hall golf course is pictured READ MORE :

Charlotte told the Metro: "A lot of us blame ourselves because Hailey doesn’t usually leave her with anybody, she goes to a special school. But the school holidays have come up and her mum was desperate for a child minder. She’d asked a Facebook group if anybody knew of any in the area."

Her dad Kieran Bradshaw has described her as his "best friend" and an "amazing daughter" in a tribute shared on Facebook. He said: "Sat here feeling so alone with everybody around us but not knowing what the rest of our lives look like without our little girl, noises around the house, songs coming on and adding them to her own Spotify playlist for the car, seeing a McDonald’s and wanting it calling out, Thursdays we’re baking days and having a right good song along while dancing.

"You were so loved Nyla you touched everyone’s heart that ever met you. I’ll never ever go a moment without you in my thoughts.

Article continues below

"You seen the world as your playground free from any worries or fears and I learnt from you in my darkest of places that your smile and outlook was something so bright and I can’t believe I’ll not hear your voice again it took a long time for you to start saying 'I love you' or 'I miss you' only a year ago.

"You are my best friend and my amazing daughter. I hope grandad had a balloon waiting for you when you meet him he will look after you."

A fundraiser has been set up on GoFundMe to support the family with funeral costs. Organisers said the family are "now facing the unimaginable pain of losing their beautiful daughter, alongside many unanswered questions and the overwhelming responsibility of arranging her funeral," the fundraiser said.

News.title: Queen's 'surprise' visits exposed by royal butler - 'She didn't shout about it'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Queen's 'surprise' visits exposed by royal butler - 'She didn't shout about it'

A former royal butler opens up about one of the late Queen's strongest and long-lasting relationships that helped her through her most testing times

View 9 Images The Queen's faith was deeply personal, according to those who witnessed it (Image: Getty Images)

In her 2014 Christmas Day broadcast, Queen Elizabeth II described Jesus Christ as “an inspiration and an anchor” in her life, adding that he was “a role model of reconciliation and forgiveness,” and he “stretched out his hands in love, acceptance and healing”.

‌



According to those who knew her best, the late Queen remained as devoted to her Christian faith as she was to the institution of monarchy and her beloved family throughout her 96 years.

‌



“Her Majesty spoke openly on many occasions of the strength she took from her Christian faith, and often turned to the teachings of the Bible at difficult moments in her own life and the life of the nation,” notes the royal family ’s website.

‌



View 9 Images The late monarch turned to her faith in some of her most difficult periods during her 70-year reign (Image: WireImage)

It adds that, in her role as Defender of the Faith and Supreme Governor of the Church of England, she “respected all faiths, seeing them as a force for good in the world, and a way of bringing communities together.”

When residing at her beloved Balmoral Castle in Scotland, the Queen attended the weekly service at the small parish church of Crathie Kirk – a tradition started by Queen Victoria some hundred years earlier.

‌



Reverend Kenneth Mackenzie, who became the minister of the Parish of Braemar and Crathie in 2005, describes how she lived a life “shaped by faith, infused with grace, and characterised by selfless service”.

Speaking shortly after her death in September 2022, he revealed that since he had been appointed as Parish minister 17 years before, “there have been only two Sundays – apart from Covid times – that she didn’t come to church.”

View 9 Images Crathie Kirk Church was a favourite of the late Queen's and she regularly attended the Sunday Service while staying at Balmoral (Image: PA)

‌



Former royal butler Grant Harrold recalls how Her Majesty often attended private services without other members of the family and away from photographers.

“I remember being surprised when I discovered that on Christmas morning she would go to a smaller service, before the main service at St Mary Magdalene in Sandringham,” he tells OK !. “It was never a secret, but she didn’t always feel the need to shout about her faith, and whenever she had an opportunity to go to church and worship alone, she would take it.”

Tessa Dunlop, a historian and royal author, believes that the late Queen was the “last generation” born with such an unwavering faith in God. She describes her faith as “deeply personal”, and understands how it would have been a great source of comfort during more challenging times.

‌



When the world was plunged into uncertainty and fear during the Covid pandemic in 2020, the Queen spoke openly about finding solace in faith, and of light being a symbol of hope.

View 9 Images Queen Elizabeth II rarely missed a Sunday service at Crathie Kirk Church in Aberdeenshire (Image: Getty Images)

During a special Easter message, recorded in isolation at Windsor Castle, she said, “The discovery of the risen Christ on the first Easter Day gave his followers new hope and fresh purpose, and we can all take heart from this. We know that Coronavirus will not overcome us. As dark as death can be – particularly for those suffering with grief – light and life are greater. May the living flame of the Easter hope be a steady guide as we face the future.”

‌



She relied on this steadying guide more than ever during her “annus horribilis” in 1992, when Windsor Castle was ravaged by fire and three of her children’s marriages broke down.

According to Tessa, the Queen “prioritised marriage as much as the monarchy,” so the separation of the then-Prince Andrew and Sarah Ferguson, followed by the divorce of Princess Anne and Captain Mark Phillips, and the public unravelling of Charles and Princess Diana ’s marriage, was deeply difficult for her to accept.

9 View 9 Images The fire at Windsor Castle destroyed the historic chapel (Image: Corbis via Getty Images) 9 View 9 Images The monarch delivered her famous 'annus horribilis' speech at Guildhall Great Hall (Image: Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)

‌



The Queen later described it as a “sombre” time, adding that it was “not a year on which I shall look back with undiluted pleasure”.

Tessa also suspects the Queen’s relationship with God was particularly significant in the days and weeks following the tragic death of Diana, Princess of Wales, in 1997.

The Queen was in Balmoral with Charles and Princes William and Harry when news arrived that her former daughter-in-law had been killed in a car crash in Paris. However, following her reluctance to immediately return to London, which was the epicentre of public mourning, she was soon faced with growing anger from the public.

‌



Tessa believes that during this period of grief and crisis, the Queen most likely sought guidance from her faith rather than from Palace advisors.

9 View 9 Images The Queen attended Princess Diana's funeral service at Westminster Abbey in September 1997 (Image: Getty Images) 9 View 9 Images This special collector's edition of OK! commemorates the 100th anniversary of Queen Elizabeth II's birth and look back on some of her most defining moments.

‌



“There’s something quite liminal about being in a place like the remote Highlands compared to the noise and bustle of London at that time,” she tells us. “To me, it showed that she needed to have a conversation with God, just to find the way forward.

“She went to the small Crathie Kirk Church the day after [Diana’s death], and it really demonstrated her connection to her faith.”

Following the death of Prince Philip in April 2021, the Queen spoke of how the loss of her husband had left a “huge void in her life”. However, during her Christmas broadcast that year, she spoke of the “comfort” she had taken from the story of Jesus’s birth and how his teachings were the “bedrock” of her faith, even when she was mourning.

‌



Former Archbishop of Canterbury Justin Welby later praised the Queen for her commitment to “doing the right thing” by sitting alone at Prince Philip’s funeral, which happened when Covid restrictions were still in place. He also described Her Majesty’s Christian faith as “the rock on which she stands”.

View 9 Images The Queen stood alone at the funeral of her late husband Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh (Image: PA)

As Grant says, the combination of the Queen’s dedication to duty and her unwavering commitment to Christianity gave her the resilience to “keep going”, regardless of the obstacles she sometimes faced.

Article continues below

“She knew that whether the monarchy was going through good times or dark times, she was not going to give up,” he says. “Even during that ‘annus horribilis’, with the splits and the fire at Windsor Castle – which was essentially the symbol of the House of Windsor burning down – she knew she was always going to find a way to keep going.

“Through fires, divorces and backlashes, her faith – and her determination to serve – never wavered.”

News.title: 'I parked in front of neighbour's house for 11 days so he took drastic action'
News.content:
'I parked in front of neighbour's house for 11 days so he took drastic action'

A man parked in front of his neighbour's house for 11 days as he saw no problem with doing so. However, it wasn't long before drastic action was taken and a row broke out

View Image He parked outside his house for 11 days (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

Sometimes it can be a nightmare to find somewhere to park, and deciding to pull up outside a neighbour's house can lead to all sorts of problems. One man recently discovered this when he opted to leave his car outside his neighbour's property for 11 days, as it led to a pretty big parking row.

‌



The man, who felt like he did nothing wrong, told the story on Reddit, as matters appeared to spiral out of control. When he returned to his car, a note was left on his windscreen from the neighbour, and it's clear his decision caused a lot of upset.

‌



In the post, it was explained the neighbour claims he " owns a street parking spot" and alleges he called the police about the matter too. It's not the first time someone has caused upset by parking in front of their neighbour's home either.

‌



The man, from Scotland, said: "Hi all, I’d appreciate some advice on a situation. I parked my car on a residential street I live across from.

"There were no yellow signs, no permit lines, not blocking any driveway. The car was left there for 11 days while I was away.

"When I came back, I found this note on my car and, as I was driving away, the person who left the note came out and kept saying 'never do this again'. I told him I was parked legally, but he kept repeating that he didn’t care and told me to 'never do that again'. The interaction felt uncomfortable and quite intimidating.

‌



"I’m trying to understand if I’ve actually done anything wrong here legally. Also, even if I’m not at fault, is there an expectation or etiquette not to park outside someone’s house if it’s the only available space?

"Also, is there any risk of me getting into legal trouble for this situation (as he mentioned contacting the police and claimed they told him I live nearby)? Thanks in advance."

‌



A picture of the note was also shared, and the neighbour deemed him an "inconsiderate driver". He also made claims he parked in a "private street" that's owned by residents, which stops people from parking there.

The man was alleged to have not considered the homeowners, which the neighbour claims caused them "stress and inconvenience." Despite this, the man who parked the car said there were "no signs" to suggest this was the case.

The situation got a lot of people talking, as hundreds commented on the post. They offered all sorts of ideas.

‌



One said: "I work in highways and deal with this stuff all the time. The road being unadopted simply means that the local highway authority doesn't maintain it.

"It could mean that another department within the council owns it. House title deeds DO show the boundary going into the road, however this does NOT mean that they 'own' the road.

"They typically own the earth underneath the road. There is usually still a public right of way and, unless the guy can prove that there is no public right of way or a parking restriction, you're free to park wherever."

‌



Another added: "I'll second this. I worked in housing and many of the estate roads were owned and maintained by the Housing Revenue. Account rather than Highways.

"Your average Joe wouldn't have seen any difference between the two and used them accordingly." A third replied: "Maybe they were annoyed you left your vehicle there for 11 days."

Meanwhile, a fourth commented: "He couldn’t do anything about it for 11 days except leave a note. If he had any powers, he would have done something about it sooner for sure."

Article continues below

One more also noted: "Whether you've done something illegal or not, I doubt the police would prosecute. However, if you don't even live down that road, it's a little inconsiderate to leave your car outside someone's house for 11 days straight."

News.title: Major rule change from today April 1 2026 affects tenants and people who own flats
News.content:
Major rule change from today April 1 2026 affects tenants and people who own flats

It aims to bring more people in

View 3 Images Keir Mather is the minister for decarbonisation (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Brits put off switching to an electric vehicle (EV) due to not having a driveway are being addressed through a regulatory amendment taking effect from Wednesday, April 1, 2026. A significant rule alteration is increasing a grant from £350 to £500.

‌



Tenants and flat owners can apply, alongside businesses, schools and other organisations. The Government indicated it would typically fund half the expense of installing an EV charger at home.

‌



For those without a driveway, it will contribute towards the expense of an alternative arrangement, such as cross-pavement chargers. Tenants, flat owners, landlords, homeowners without driveways and businesses are all eligible.

‌



Keir Mather, the minister for decarbonisation, told BBC Radio 4's You and Yours programme at the end of February, when the changes were first announced: "We think it will make a big difference. We are working as hard as possible so that as many people as possible can make the switch to an electric vehicle, but we can only do that if we make it cost-effective to charge from home.

"So by uplifting this grant from £350 to 500, that's going to cover almost half the cost of the typical install of a charge point, about 42% of the cost. But the important point is installing those charge points unlocks those massive cost savings that you can get through home charging of around 2p a mile.

View 3 Images It's simple if you've got a drive, not as much otherwise (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"So that's the equivalent of driving from London to Birmingham for about £3.50. We want as many people as possible to be able to access that, and that's why we're extending the grant today."

Tina McKenzie, policy chair at the Federation of Small Businesses, said: "Many small businesses want to switch to electric vehicles, with half of small businesses (51%) saying that more charging infrastructure would incentivise them to make the switch.

"Small firms want to cut their emissions and reduce their fuel bills and removing or lowering the barriers which currently tip the scales against electric vehicle adoption can only be a good thing – for small businesses, for the economy and for the planet."

‌



View 3 Images The idea is to make charging an EV easier, especially if you don't have a driveway (Image: Pexels)

Ben Beadle, chief executive of the National Residential Landlords Association, said: "Almost nine in 10 landlords with a suitable property would install EV charge points if a tenant asks them to undertake this work.

"Given the extent of landlords' willingness to provide them, we welcome the government's plans to encourage more widespread installation of these points across the sector. We urge landlords to make best use of the grants now available where it is feasible for them to do so."

Article continues below

Details on how to apply can be found at gov.uk.

News.title: Brit oil company 'hit by Iranian drone' in Iraq as footage shows massive blaze
News.content:
Massive plumes of smoke appear to be coming from a British motor oil company hit by drones as the Middle East conflict rages on.

A Castrol oil plant, in the city of Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region, Iraq, is reportedly on fire after being struck. It comes after Seyed Ali Mousavi, Tehran’s ambassador to the UK, said Iran is considering strikes on British military bases.

Like other neighbouring countries to Iran, Iraq has been dragged into the conflict that began on February 28, and has been regularly targeted by drone attacks.

Image: Rudaw English/X) Rudaw English/X)

Disruptions to gulf shipping and attacks on oil infrastructure has all that made it impossible for Iraq to export crude, jeopardizing the country that relies on this export for the bulk of its revenue.

A drone strike triggered the large fire at Castrol oil warehouses operated by the Sardar Group on the Erbil–Mosul road.

A company source told Shafaq News that the drone fell inside the facility, igniting a blaze that engulfed large quantities of oil and logistical materials with emergency services working to bring the fire under control.

The damage is described as extensive due to the highly flammable nature of the stored materials, while it is understood that no staff at the site were injured.

Erbil governor Omid Xoshnaw said the first drone attack took place at around 7.30am which targeted a depot storing the automotive motor oil.

And with fire fighters tackling the blaze, further drone strikes hit the same location at around 8.40am and 10.20am. Mr Xoshnaw said that a total of three drones hit the facility directly, while a fourth drone was intercepted and detonated mid-air before reaching its target.

“The repeated bombardment and the scale of the fire have left nothing inside the depot untouched by flames,” Mr Xoshnaw told Kurdistan24, adding that emergency personnel were later instructed to withdraw from the immediate area due to safety concerns.

Iran's ambassador to the UK, Mr Mousavi, says that his country is considering attacks on British military bases due to involvement in the war.

“The initial position made by Prime Minister Starmer is very good,” he told Times Radio. “We do appreciate (it), we do welcome the non-involvement in this criminal act of the American side and the Israeli regime.

“But unfortunately, now we have realised that the British Fairford military base has been serving for the B2 and B1, you know, jets of the American side to be equipped by the different weapons to use against the Iranian people. It’s very unfortunate.”

Asked whether British bases and assets were “legitimate targets”, Mr Mousavi replied: “This is the very important matter we are considering. This is a very important matter for our self-defence.”

He added Iranian military authorities “will decide appropriately” what course of action they will take, adding any final decision “depends on” UK activities.
